newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may not issue another '97 Eurobond - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia may not issue another '97 Eurobond - minister.

text.p: Russia may not issue another Eurobond in 1997 as tax collection is rising, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Monday.
"By the end of the year Russia may not issue any more bonds as the situation with tax collection is improving," Kasyanov, in charge of Russia's foreign debt, told Reuters.
Interfax news agency quoted First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin as saying that Russia would not issue its fourth Eurobond if tax collection improved.

A State Tax Service official told Reuters tax collection in the first five months was 85 percent of the budget forecast after 69 percent in the first quarter. She said June tax collection was even better, but the exact figure was not yet available.
Russia has said it planned to make a global issue this autumn and dealers estimated the volume would be between $500 million and $1 billion.
Russia placed its third, $2.0 billion, Eurobond in June. Finance Ministry officials previously said some of the proceeds were used to pay pension arrears.
